title: Add retention-labeled audit middleware and RBACv2 transient bindings
author: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Customers and internal compliance teams requested finer-grained control over how audit records are retained and routed depending on data residency/tenant constraints and transient operator scopes. Existing audit pipeline attached a single retention policy per-tenant which made temporary operator actions (eg emergency operator fixes) either over-retain or under-retain sensitive entries, and RBACv2 transient bindings were not annotated for audit delivery that respects retention labels.

Solution: This PR introduces a small pluggable middleware in the api-gateway/audit path that labels audit records with an explicit retention class (P0/P1/ephemeral) derived from combined inputs: tenant policy, request-scoped operator binding, and optional KMS affinity headers. In parallel this change adds a new RBACv2 transient-binding type that carries a short TTL and a retention_preference attribute. The middleware consults the rbac service for transient-binding metadata, merges it with tenant policy (tenant-level minimums are enforced), and emits an audit envelope with retention_label and delivery_hint metadata. The delivery pipeline can then route short-lived envelopes to the ephemeral-store and mark persistent ones for long-term retention.

This PR contains: 1) API changes to RBAC service to expose transient-binding metadata (read-only surface used by middleware), 2) gateway middleware that annotates audit envelopes, 3) audit-forwarder modifications to inspect retention_label and route to ephemeral vs durable stores, 4) a short e2e smoke test and unit tests for merge logic, 5) docs and release notes describing the new retention classes and operational knobs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add retention_label plumbing in api-gateway middleware
- [x] Add transient-binding TTL and retention_preference field to RBACv2 schema (backwards compatible)
- [x] Ensure tenant-level minimum retention enforced (rejects shorter TTL than tenant min)
- [x] Audit-forwarder routing based on retention_label and delivery_hint
- [x] Unit tests and integration smoke test
- [x] Console docs draft and changelog entry

Backward compatibility: New RBAC transient-binding field is optional and defaults to null; any binding without retention_preference is treated as 'tenant-default'. Audit envelope schema adds optional retention_label/delivery_hint - older consumers ignore unknown fields. Rollout: feature gated behind flag feature.audit_retention and toggled off by default. We plan a staged rollout: gate flipped in staging for 48h, then Canary, then global.

Motivation and security considerations: the retention label is a conservative opt-in from transient operator bindings; tenant policy always wins when it requires longer retention to meet compliance. We explicitly disallow extension of retention by transient bindings (i.e., an operator cannot force longer retention than tenant min). We added integration tests exercising KMS affinity header usage to ensure audit routing metadata cannot be spoofed without proper authenticated KMS tokens.

Notes: This is primarily an infra and compliance surface change; no user-visible API surface changes except RBACv2 schema extension which is backward compatible. See release_notes for operator actions required when upgrading dedicated/private clusters (RBAC schema migration job included).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial rbac schema add (transient-binding fields); middleware implementation and unit tests; audit-forwarder routing change; e2e smoke test and test data; docs and changelog prep. Examples: 'rbac: add transient_binding retention_preference+ttl', 'gateway: add audit retention middleware', 'forwarder: route ephemeral envelopes to ephemeral-store', 'tests: add retention merge logic tests'.

Priya Desai: Added test 'TestMergeRespectsTenantMin' and updated rbacschema migration notes. Also added a guard to reject transient bindings that attempt to set ttl < tenantMin.
Sofia Martinez: The migration SQL could block in older clusters - suggest a non-blocking background migration and feature flag. Can we add a migration plan in deploy docs?

Priya Desai: Replaced postgres-backed test with in-memory forwarder harness; re-run CI.

testing_notes: Unit tests added for merge logic and tenant minimum enforcement. Forwarder tests use in-memory harness to verify routing. A small e2e smoke test deploys gateway+forwarder to test namespace and verifies ephemeral vs durable buckets receive expected envelope counts. Canary run in us-west-2 for 48h showed 0 failures and expected retention label distribution. Manual security review verified KMS affinity token signature check.
release_notes: Introduce audit retention labels and RBACv2 transient-binding TTL/retention_preference. Feature gated behind 'feature.audit_retention'. Operators must run the provided non-blocking migration if upgrading clusters older than 2026-02 and review console changes for transient binding creation. See docs/ops/audit_retention.md for migration steps and operational guidance.
notes_for_ops: When enabling feature.audit_retention: 1) Ensure background migration script '2026-02-rbac-transient-bindings-async.sql' is scheduled; 2) Confirm ephemeral store (S3 prefix or ephemeral DB) configured for locality-sensitive ephemeral audit; 3) Monitor 'audit.retention.label' metric and set alerts if >5% of operator actions are labeled 'ephemeral' unexpectedly.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: Behavioral change limited to audit routing. Tenant min retention enforces conservative behavior. Migration is non-blocking and feature is gated. Added extra validations to prevent escalation via transient bindings and KMS affinity tokens require signature verification.
